Thanks again for the SIG we received. Our security team has a handful of follow-ups specifically about incident response and breach notification timelines. Can you please confirm the items below? We attached our SIG extract with the relevant sections for convenience (acme-sig-questions.pdf).

1) Detection and confirmation: typical detection-to-confirmation median time for a security incident involving customer data?
2) Initial customer notification: maximum time after confirmation that Redwood commits to notifying impacted customers (we're particularly concerned about GDPR 72-hour windows).
3) Regulatory/legal notification: do you have a commitment or escalation path for law enforcement/regulator notification — who signs off?
4) Contacts & escalation: primary IR contact, backup, and privacy/legal contact for notifications (preferred email + phone).
5) Evidence preservation: are forensics preserved and for how long (logs, images, packet captures)? Where is SOC2 test evidence stored for auditors to review?
6) Do you have a standard customer-facing incident notice template we can review?

If you can provide a short written response plus any templates (notice template, IR checklist) that would be very helpful. We need answers by the end of next week if possible.

Best,

Maria — hi, Laura from Security & Compliance here. Thanks for the questions — answers below are written to be concise for your SIG. I've attached a filled PDF with the SIG IR section completed (SIG-IR-answers.pdf) and a customer incident notice template (redwood-incident-notice-template.docx).

1) Detection -> confirmation: median detection time varies by class of event. For infrastructure/service alarms (e.g., anomalous process/excessive API errors) median detection is ~1.5 hours; for subtle data-exfiltration patterns median detection can be up to 24–48 hours depending on telemetry.

2) Initial customer notification: Our policy is to notify impacted customers within 72 hours of confirmation for incidents where personal data is implicated. For incidents that are still under active investigation with incomplete scope, we will send an initial factual notification within 72 hours and follow-ups as scope is confirmed. This is aligned with GDPR guidance; we do not guarantee public disclosure timelines for non-personal-data outages (those follow standard incident status updates).

3) Regulatory/legal notification: Legal signs off on statutory/regulator notifications. Our escalation policy is: Incident Commander (Security) -> Head of Security (Laura Bennett) -> General Counsel. We will involve Law Enforcement only under a legal compulsion or in coordination with customer request.

4) Contacts & escalation: primary IR contact: security@redwood.com (monitored 24/7); backup on-call: +1 (650) 555-0999 (redwood SOC on-call). For privacy/legal: legal@redwood.com; Senior privacy lead: Vivek Kulkarni (vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com). For immediate escalation, call the on-call number.

5) Evidence preservation: We preserve event logs, relevant VM snapshots, and application-level traces for a minimum of 90 days by default; raw packet capture is retained for 14 days unless specifically preserved for a forensic investigation. For forensic requests tied to formal audits we retain and export encrypted artifacts; retention can be extended under contractual agreement. SOC 2 control test artifacts are made available to authorized auditors via a secured Drive location (link below).

6) Customer-facing notice template: attached (redwood-incident-notice-template.docx). The template includes a factual summary, impacted services, timeline, mitigation steps, and contact information.

Sample short timeline (for SIG context):
- T0: Detection alert (timestamp)
- T+1–24h: Triage and scope assessment
- T+24–72h: Confirmation and initial customer notification (if personal data impacted)
- T+72h+: Detailed follow-up with root cause and remediation plan as scope is validated

Attachments: SIG-IR-answers.pdf (filled answers), redwood-incident-notice-template.docx

If you need us to sign specific SLA language or a short rider about notification timing, we can route that to Legal; please send the clause.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Head of Security & Compliance — Redwood Inference

Maria — a few technical clarifications to supplement Laura's note:

- Detection tooling: we use a layered approach (host EDR, centralized SIEM, anomaly detectors in our serving runtime) and aggregate alerts into the Incident Response platform.
- Forensics preservation: when an incident is confirmed we snapshot the affected instances (immutable encrypted images) and export relevant logs to our secure forensics bucket. Images are kept as long as the investigation requires; default retention for exported artifacts is 90 days unless extended by Legal/Customer requirement.
- Time-to-detect examples from past operational incidents: median 2.1 hours for runtime anomalies; median 16 hours for stealthy exfiltration patterns once aggregated telemetry triggers correlate events.
- SOC 2 evidence: control test artifacts and evidence are maintained in our internal compliance Drive and are shared with customers/auditors via a secure link after NDA/approval. Example link: https://drive.google.com/redwood/shared/IR-evidence-location

Contact for forensics exports: forensics@redwood.com (ticket-based; we prioritize requests tied to live investigations).

—Evelyn
